verdicts.question: Has the Karnataka Platform-Based Gig Workers (Social Security and Welfare) Act 2025 been brought into force with rules, what welfare-fee rates and categories were notified (Feb 2026), and what is the status of the reported 2026 Karnataka High Court challenge?
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION NOT POSSIBLE ON THIS MACHINE: the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before this sceptic pass began and page fetches are refused, so none of the 14 cited sources could be confirmed by any snippet; the three earlier 'verify:gig-workers' runs in the workflow journal (wf_08eff266-1e1) all failed with no output, so no prior snippet check exists either. Per the brief's rule, an answer whose key claims are unsupported by any snippet found defaults to holds=false; this is a verification failure, not a discovered error. Items that remain 'not confirmed by snippet': the Act number 72 of 2025 and the 11/12 Sep 2025 assent/gazette dates; 'deemed in force from 30 May 2025'; the Rules notification LD 413 LET 2023 of 19 Nov 2025 (Gazette Part IVA No. 739); the '16-member' Board constituted 27 Jan 2026; the full 13 Feb 2026 rate table (1% with caps Rs 0.50/0.75/1.00/1.50 by category and vehicle); Rule 17's exclusion of tips/incentives; every High Court detail (WP 19746/2026, Justice M. Nagaprasanna, 3 Jul 2026 refusal of stay, 23 Jul deposit date, 31 Jul/10 Aug/14 Aug timetable, Uber's WP 19776/2026 before Justice Suraj Govindaraj on 28 Jul, notice returnable 24 Aug); and the 31 Aug 2026 Medianama figures (about Rs 4 crore deposited, 15 platforms, 7 lakh workers, Yulu paying directly, Uber/Eternal/Porter resigning). INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES FOUND IN THE REPO: (1) the sibling risk-guards answer (question 7, same 29 Sep run, citing Business Standard of 8 Jul 2026) says the High Court refused a stay on 8 Jul 2026, this answer says 3 Jul 2026 — one of the two is wrong, or 8 Jul is the article date; (2) risk-guards says the fee was 'notified on 16 Feb 2026, effective 13 Feb 2026' while this answer says the order was 'issued on 13 Feb 2026'; (3) the answer's own ThePrint source is titled 'aggregators to contribute 1-1.5% welfare fee per transaction', which contradicts the answer's 'every notified category at 1%' unless the headline refers to rupee caps — unresolved; (4) risk-guards and support-ops cite The South First (31 Mar 2026) for a 7-working-day filing / 15-working-day resolution grievance timeline under the Rules, whereas this answer gives 14-day action-taken report and 45-day final order under the Act (s.22) — both may be true (Rules vs Act) but they must be reconciled in one place. Arithmetic and date math check out (see correction). NEWER DEVELOPMENTS: could not be searched; the answer itself admits the 14 Aug and 24 Aug 2026 listings are unreported, so the status 'answered' overstates what is known — the last confirmed court event in the answer is 28 Jul 2026, two months before the pilot. REFINED-CHAIN FIT: the answer predates the 30 Sep chain refinement and needs the changes listed in the correction.
verdicts.correction: Keep the substance but downgrade status from 'answered' to 'partly' and edit as follows. (a) Say plainly that as of 30 Sep 2026 the Act, Rules, Board and 13 Feb 2026 fee order are reported in force, that the High Court has not stayed the Act, and that the outcome of the 14 Aug 2026 (IAMAI batch) and 24 Aug 2026 (Uber) listings is unknown; pin the stay-refusal date only after reconciling 3 Jul (this answer, LiveLaw/Medianama) against 8 Jul (risk-guards answer, Business Standard), and pin the fee order as 'dated 13 Feb 2026, reported 16 Feb 2026' rather than asserting one date. (b) Mark the per-category cap table as 'as reported by The News Minute / SCC Online / United Consultancy, not checked against the gazette order', and note the ThePrint '1-1.5%' headline as an unexplained discrepancy to clear with the Board. (c) Arithmetic that does hold: 1% of a payout is capped at Rs 0.50 once the payout exceeds Rs 50, so at pilot scale the cap binds on almost every pickup; 10 Saathis x 20 jobs x 26 days = 5,200 jobs x Rs 0.50 = Rs 2,600 a month — 'a few thousand rupees a month' is right. (d) Refined chain: Saathi work now spans pickups from households AND from kabadiwalas, yards, pre-processors, dry-waste centres/MRFs and industrial by-product generators (bagasse, fly ash, slag, foundry sand etc.), much of which moves by 3W, LCV or HCV, so the budget line must use the higher caps (Rs 0.75 / 1.00 / 1.50 per job) for those jobs and the Saathi job record must carry vehicle class and the material state at handover (S0/S1 for household pickups, S2-S3 for yard-to-pre-processor moves); sorting shifts at yards, pre-processors and MRFs are fixed-location work that fits none of the Karnataka Schedule's eight rows cleanly (Form A's 'Warehousing' row is the closest) and, being shift-based rather than per-job, has no obvious 'transaction' to cap — record each shift as one transaction and ask the Board to confirm. No welfare fee arises on pure goods trades between businesses (L2-L5 price levels) because no gig worker is party to them; the fee attaches only to Saathi payouts. Open items: outcome of the 14 Aug and 24 Aug 2026 hearings; whether rates exist for the healthcare, travel-and-hospitality and content-and-media rows; the gazette text of the 13 Feb 2026 order.

verdicts.question: Is a scrap-pickup marketplace or a Saathi job board an 'aggregator' or 'e-marketplace' under the Karnataka Act and under the Social Security Code's Seventh Schedule and the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026, if the kabadiwala pays the Saathi directly rather than the platform? If so, which fee category, who pays, and does the internal dispute committee duty apply?
verdicts.problems: VERIFICATION NOT POSSIBLE ON THIS MACHINE (search budget exhausted, fetches refused; no earlier verify run succeeded), so every citation is 'not confirmed by snippet': the Karnataka Act section numbers relied on (s.1(3)(ii), s.2(b),(e),(f),(g), s.14, s.15, s.17, s.18, s.20(1),(5), s.21 proviso, s.22(2),(4),(6), s.23) and the exact wording of 'aggregator', 'platform' and 'payout'; the Rules numbers (Rule 7(2)(h), 7(7), 8, 11(1),(3), 13, 17, 20, 21, 22(2), 29) and Form A's 'Warehousing' and 'Any other' rows; the IDRC composition (1 chair + 2 management + at least 3 senior gig workers, at least 2 women); the Social Security (Central) Rules 2026 as G.S.R. 344(E) of 8 May 2026 with Rules 48(2)(b),(c), 49(2),(5) and Forms XX/XXI, the 30 June / 31 October filing dates and 1% per month interest; and the claim that the s.114 contribution commencement has not been notified as of September 2026 (Taxmann source dated only '2026-09'). What does hold structurally from the Code's text as enacted: the s.2 'aggregator' definition (digital intermediary or marketplace connecting buyer/user with seller/service provider), the Seventh Schedule's nine categories including a residual 'any other goods and services provider platform', and s.114(4)'s 1-2% of turnover capped at 5% of amounts paid or payable to gig and platform workers. Sibling research in the repo (legal brief and risk-guards, 29 Sep) independently states the Code came into force on 21 Nov 2025 and that the central Rules of 8 May 2026 require registration on the Shram Suvidha portal, a 45-day upload of existing workers and real-time joins/exits — consistent with this answer, but from the same day's searches, so it is corroboration of consistency, not of truth. Date math checks: 8 May 2026 + 45 days = 22 Jun 2026, as stated. Two things the answer under-states: (1) the sibling risk-guards answer gives a 7-working-day / 15-working-day grievance timeline from the Rules that this answer omits alongside the Act's 14-day / 45-day steps — reconcile; (2) Saathis' own e-Shram self-registration (the legal brief's 90/120-day benefit clock) is missing from the compliance list. The 'payout' analysis for the direct-pay model is reasoned rather than sourced and is correctly parked with counsel. REFINED-CHAIN FIT: the answer treats Saathi work as household pickups plus sorting for kabadiwalas; the refined chain adds engagers (yards, pre-processors, MRFs/dry-waste centres, industrial by-product generators) and heavier vehicles, which changes the fee category mix and the 'who pays' analysis — see correction.
verdicts.correction: Keep the conclusion (treat Luma.Green as an aggregator and a platform under both regimes from 13 Oct 2026 regardless of who pays the Saathi; constitute the IDRC; register on both portals) and the 'needs-pilot-or-counsel' status, but edit as follows. (a) Label every section and rule number as 'to be confirmed against the gazette text by counsel' — none could be checked here — and add the e-Shram self-registration duty for Saathis (benefits after 90 days with one aggregator or 120 days across several, per the sibling legal brief) plus the Rules' 7-working-day / 15-working-day grievance timeline next to the Act's 14-day / 45-day steps, or state which governs. (b) Fee categories under the refined chain: household pickups (S0 to S1) on 2W = Logistics 2W, cap Rs 0.50; collection runs from kabadiwalas to yards and yard-to-pre-processor lot moves (S2/S3) mostly on 3W/LCV = Logistics 3W Rs 0.75 or LCV Rs 1.00; industrial by-product pickups (bagasse, fly ash, slag, foundry sand, husk) on LCV/HCV = Rs 1.00-1.50; sorting shifts at yards, pre-processors and MRFs are fixed-location, shift-paid work with no natural per-transaction unit — book one shift as one transaction under the closest row (Form A 'Warehousing' or 'Any other'), cap Rs 1.50 assumed, and get the Board's written confirmation. Record vehicle class, engager type and material state on every Saathi job so the cap is computable per row. (c) Who pays: the fee is on Luma.Green as aggregator/platform in every case; the engager (kabadiwala, yard, pre-processor, MRF, brand/PRO, TSDF) never pays it and cannot be charged it, though Luma.Green may price it into its own service fee. No fee attaches to the goods trades themselves at L2-L5 because no gig worker is a party. (d) Payout base: when a yard or pre-processor pays a Saathi in cash or UPI outside the app, the s.2(f) 'payout' gap the answer identifies is wider than for kabadiwalas, so the pilot should require every engager to record the Saathi payment in-app (amount, mode, job) and treat that record as the payout; ask counsel whether the engager, not Luma.Green, could instead be the 'aggregator' when it is itself a registered business hiring shifts. (e) Budget stays near the answer's figure for a 2W-only pilot (about Rs 2,600 a month at 5,200 jobs) but rises to roughly Rs 5,200-7,800 a month if the same job count moves on LCV/HCV, still immaterial. Open items unchanged: s.2(f) payout on direct pay, Schedule row for sorting, s.114(5) commencement, portal name and interim self-report format.
